title: audit-finding
description: A single severity-tagged finding emitted by the audit sub-agent. Conforms to the structure mandated by core/audit/prompts/system.md Step 4 and the V1.1-AUDIT.md report style.

id.description: Stable identifier in <DIM>-<NNN> form (ADOPT-02 v1.1.1). DIM is a 2-8 char uppercase token naming the finding domain (e.g. SEC, PE, AUDIT, INPUT); NNN is a 3-digit zero-padded counter monotonically incremented within a single report. The dimension token carries no severity semantics.

cycle.description: Audit cycle counter (ADOPT-02 v1.1.1). 1 = first audit pass; 2 = re-audit after implementer addressed cycle-1 findings; 3 = final retry. After cycle 3 a finding MUST be ESCALATED rather than re-cycled — escalation forces a human decision instead of perpetual loops.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the finding (ADOPT-02 v1.1.1). OPEN = newly emitted, awaiting fix; IN-PROGRESS = implementer is actively addressing it; RESOLVED = fix verified by re-audit; ESCALATED = unresolved after cycle 3 (human owner required); ACCEPTED-RISK = explicit human sign-off to ship without fix (allowed only for MEDIUM/LOW/INFO; CRITICAL/HIGH retain zero-deferral).

severity.description: Severity level on the charter v1.1 §6.1 scale. CRITICAL and HIGH are zero-deferral. Auditor MUST NOT downshift severity to make merge easier (severity-laundering guard).

dimension.description: Audit dimension. Pick the dimension that primarily describes the defect; allow a second finding under the other dimension only when the framings genuinely differ (panel:E3 row 18, 60-70% overlap expected).

where.description: Location of the defect. Must be a concrete file:line range the auditor has personally Read; orphan findings (no file:line) are forbidden.

line_end.description: 1-indexed inclusive end line. Equals line_start for a single-line finding.

secondary_files.description: Additional files implicated by the finding. Useful when a defect spans multiple files; the primary file:line stays in line_start/line_end.

description.description: One paragraph: what the code does, why it is wrong against the spec or threat-model, why this severity. No prose flourishes; evidence-grounded.

recommended_fix.description: One paragraph: what the implementer should change. Concrete; reference function names or line numbers where possible. Auditor does NOT modify code; this is guidance only.

references.description: Sources cited in support of this finding. Mix of panel finding IDs (e.g. 'panel:E1 F5'), charter sections (e.g. 'charter v1.1 §2.3'), checklist items (e.g. 'security-checklist A1'), and external URLs.

checklist_item.description: Optional pointer to the specific checklist line item that was marked [!] for this finding (e.g. 'A1', 'P3'). Aids traceability between Checklist section and Findings table in the report.

evidence.description: Optional excerpt of the offending code (≤200 chars) and an optional grep/glob query the auditor used to corroborate. NOT for prose narrative.

verified_via.description: How the auditor confirmed (e.g. 'Read auth/handler.go:138-152', 'Grep for f-string in handler files').

tags.description: Optional free-form tags. Helps downstream filtering. Case-preserving (e.g. `OWASP:A03`, `STRIDE:E`, or lowercase `pii:high`, `cwe-89`).
